public_rationale: Compute Atlas's October 2, 2026 account attributes to Epoch AI an estimate of 421 MW of operating IT capacity at Abilene as of July 28, 2026 [e2]. It does not establish the operational share across the Oracle–OpenAI arrangement on a matching 7.1 GW basis [e2]. TechCrunch reported on September 10, 2025, citing the Wall Street Journal, that purchases under the five-year deal would begin in 2027 [e1]. That conflicts with the claimed June 2026 start, but does not establish the contract terms applicable in July 2026 [e1]. OpenAI's July 22, 2025 announcement concerns 4.5 GW of additional capacity to be developed, not a verified 7.1 GW denominator or July 2026 operational total [e3].
limitations: No verified operational total by July 28, 2026 matches the claimed denominator in customer scope and power definition.
The Abilene figure is a retrospective secondary account of a site estimate.
No underlying contract or amendments establish the intended commencement date and delivery schedule; commencement need not mean full-capacity delivery.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Oracle has only 5.6% of the 7.1GW needed for its OpenAI deal, which was meant to begin in June 2026.

statement.excerpt: Oracle is burning its company to the ground to build data centers for OpenAI in pursuit of a $300 billion, five-year-long compute deal that was meant to begin in June 2026 and currently has 5.6% of the 7.1GW of capacity it needs to make that revenue
statement.document_title: The More You Buy, The More You Lose

our_interpretation: The assessed proposition concerns operational Oracle capacity available to OpenAI and the stated contract start. The surrounding financial rhetoric and deal valuation are background, not separate scored propositions.
Currently means the operational state at publication. I use July 1–28, 2026 as the current reporting window, with evidence required to establish the state by July 28.
The numerator and denominator must use the same power definition and cover the same Oracle–OpenAI arrangement.
The stated percentage implies approximately 397.6MW: 7,100MW multiplied by 0.056. This arithmetic is a test threshold, not independent evidence.
A contract beginning in June 2026 does not by itself imply that all contracted capacity was required on that date.
criteria.support_condition: Reliable records establish approximately 5.6% operational capacity on a consistent 7.1GW basis at publication and establish June 2026 as the intended start of the same contract.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable records establish a materially different operational share at publication, a different contracted capacity requirement, or a different intended start date for the same agreement.

evidence.locator: Opening discussion, paragraph beginning As of the most recent public estimate
evidence.explanation: The surrounding paragraph attributes 421MW of July IT capacity to Epoch, while the article distinguishes IT load from facility power. This challenges the three-building premise but does not supply a matching 7.1GW denominator or verified customer-wide operating total.
This establishes an earlier development commitment. It does not establish 7.1GW of comparable contracted capacity or the amount operating in July 2026.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Verified records of operational Oracle capacity allocated to OpenAI by July 28, 2026 and the contracted capacity requirement on the same power basis, plus contract records establishing the intended start date and delivery schedule.
